_readme: Per-character combat skills, unlocked by levelling. Edit this file, then run Prince's Palace > Build Default Content. These are DIFFERENT from spells.json: that is one global power curve every character shares, which only changes the name and number of the single Skill button. These are a character's own kit, shown as their own row of buttons in a fight. id, displayName and characterId are always required. unlockLevel defaults to 1. effect is one of DamageSingle (default), DamageAll, HealSelf, HealParty, RestorePartyMana; targeting is inferred from the effect and rarely needs writing. Damage is (Attack, scaled by the caster's own weapon or spell scaling depending on scalingAxis, + flatAmount + power x (resource spent), minus the target's Defense unless ignoresDefense is set, floored at 1) x10 — health pools are on a x10 scale and stat-derived damage is scaled to match (CombatMath.DamageScale). damageInstances is the exception: a list of {type, amount} packets written directly on the final scale and NOT multiplied, each one checked against the target's weakness and resistance on its own, so one cast can land at +50% and -50% at the same time. Heals and mana restores are flatAmount + power x (resource spent). Costs: manaCost and/or resourceCost, and a skill must cost SOMETHING. resourceCost spends the owner's signature resource (Shawn's Wool); set spendsAllResource to take the lot, in which case resourceCost is the minimum needed to cast at all. power scales per point actually spent, so a skill with power but no resource cost is rejected rather than silently scaling by zero. Two skills for the same character MAY share an unlockLevel — Shawn opens with three. Presentation is authored here too and is entirely optional: vfxPath is a Resources folder of animation frames named f0..fN, vfxSeconds is how long the whole sequence takes, and sfxPath is a Resources path to the clip that plays when the skill lands. Any of them left out simply means no visual or no sound — never an error. scalingAxis is Auto (default, derives Weapon-vs-Spell from the caster's own attackType), Weapon, Spell, or None — override it when a skill's flavour does not match the caster's own type (a physical move authored on a Nature-typed caster, say). requires is a list of "<ability score> <amount>" lines (e.g. "strength 15") gating whether the skill can be cast at all, from base scores/talents/worn gear — empty means always castable once unlocked.

skills.description: Cut the fleece loose and let it fly. Costs no mana at all, only wool.
Chew, breathe, and let the fleece knit the day back together.
All that wool has to discharge somewhere, and it is not fussy about where.
Head down. Armour is a suggestion.
Everything he has been saving, spent at once, and it comes back to him.
A single white line from the ceiling to whatever is standing under it.
Burns and freezes in the same breath. Something out there hates one half of it.
A bark and a shake, and the whole squad finds a little more in the tank.
A warning bite, mostly.
Goes for the tendon. Armour has nothing to say about it, and neither does whatever it was about to do.
Calls the whole pack down on everything standing.
Quick, and the venom does the rest of the work.
Enough venom in one bite that armour stops being relevant.
Everything in the sac, delivered at once.
Pull in, and let the shell do what it does.
Slow to arrive. Nothing is standing where it lands.
Every hit it has taken, given back to the whole squad as reason to keep standing.
Sees the opening before it closes, and leaves it wide for whoever swings next.
Knows exactly what the squad is short on.
Everything it has seen coming, spent on making sure the squad is still there for it.
Head down, eyes up. Whatever it was going to do, it is going to do it to you.
Not elegant. Puts them at the back of the line thinking about it.
Three turns of something the fleece was hiding.
A turn of the fleece, wrapped tight. The next blow finds wool before it finds her.
Every ward she has out, broken at once, and every splinter goes somewhere.
A sound nothing in the room wants to swing through.
She has more wool than she has turns. Somebody else can have the difference.
Wound up like a spring, and pointed at something.
Go. Now. Do not wait for your turn.
